title: Monorepo scaffold & toolchain
body:
## Context
CandleViewer today contains planning documents only — there is no `package.json`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, `turbo.json` or `pyproject.toml` in the tree (`AGENTS.md` §4 status note). Every other R0 epic (E03 CI/CD, E05 design system, E06 engine spike, E07 storage spike, E08 ingestion) is blocked on a working workspace: `30-release-roadmap.md` §11.1 encodes `E01 --> E02 --> E03`, `E02 --> E05`, `E02 --> E06`, `E02 --> E07`, `E02 --> E08`, and §12 puts E02 first on the critical path `E02 → E06 → E11 → E12 → E18 → E26 → E38 → E44 → E46 → GA`.

This epic creates the repository skeleton described in `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §5 (monorepo layout) and makes the module boundaries of `CONSTITUTION.md` §3 (M1–M24 backend modules, the five frontend package rules C-3.5) **machine-enforced** from the first commit via `import-linter` and `dependency-cruiser`, so boundary rot can never start. It also delivers the local runtime (`docker compose` on WSL Ubuntu: api, postgres, questdb, grafana, prometheus, minio) so engineers and the CI integration job have an identical stack.

Scope per `30-release-roadmap.md` §4.2: "pnpm workspace + uv/poetry Python workspace; packages `chart-engine`, `protocol`, `ui`, `app-web`, `app-electron`; services `api`; `import-linter` contracts encoding `CONSTITUTION.md` §3 module edges; ESLint/Prettier/Biome, ruff, mypy strict, pytest, vitest; commitlint + husky; `.editorconfig`; Docker Compose for WSL Ubuntu" — 42 pts, sprints S01–S02.

References: `docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md`, `docs/plan/20-architecture.md#5-monorepo-layout`, `/CONSTITUTION.md` §3 and §9, `/AGENTS.md` §4.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Root pnpm workspace + Turborepo task graph implementing **every** task name in `AGENTS.md` §4 (`pnpm lint`, `lint:fix`, `format`, `typecheck`, `test`, `test:cov`, `build`, `size`, `generate`, `verify`).
- `packages/config` shared ESLint flat config, Prettier, tsconfig bases, Vitest preset.
- Package skeletons: `packages/chart-engine`, `packages/ui`, `packages/protocol`, `packages/fixtures`, `packages/config`.
- App skeletons: `apps/web` (Vite + React 18 + TS), `apps/desktop` (Electron shell, no business logic).
- `services/api` Python package skeleton with module directories M1–M24 per `CONSTITUTION.md` §3, composition root `app.py`, `settings.py` (module **M1 `config`**), `uv` + Hatch project, ruff/black/mypy-strict/pytest.
- `import-linter` contracts encoding the M1–M24 allowed-dependency table and C-3.2/C-3.3; `dependency-cruiser` + `no-restricted-imports` for TS (C-3.5, deep-import ban).
- commitlint + husky + lint-staged + `.editorconfig` + `scripts/check-agents-commands.mjs`.
- `infra/compose/` docker-compose for WSL Ubuntu: api, postgres, questdb, grafana, prometheus, minio; `.env.example`; `make up|dev|test|gen`.
- Protocol generation pipeline (`pnpm generate`) from `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` + `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` with a staleness check.
- Coverage gates wired locally at the thresholds of `CONSTITUTION.md` §9 (#3 ≥85% backend, #4 ≥85% engine, #5 ≥80% web/ui).
- ADR-0016 "Monorepo tooling and task graph"; QA, security and design-handoff tickets listed in §Story list of this body.

## Out of scope
- GitHub Actions workflows, merge queue, branch protection, deploy jobs — **E03**.
- Prometheus dashboards/alert rules and structlog redaction implementation — **E04** (this epic only starts the containers).
- Actual design tokens, components, Storybook content — **E05** (this epic provides the package and token-build wiring only).
- Any chart-engine rendering code — **E06**/**E11**; any Bybit code — **E08**.
- Alembic migrations content and QuestDB DDL — **E07**.
- Android/mobile targets, a separate admin app, non-Bybit exchanges (C-1.2).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Given a clean clone of the repository on WSL Ubuntu with pnpm, Node LTS, uv and Docker installed
When an engineer runs `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm verify`
Then every task named in AGENTS.md §4 exists and the whole gate exits 0 in under 10 minutes

Given the scaffold is merged
When a developer adds an import from services/api/oms into services/api/secrets
Then the `architecture` check (import-linter contract for C-3.2) fails with a named contract violation

Given the scaffold is merged
When a developer adds `import { x } from "apps/web/src/.."` inside packages/ui
Then dependency-cruiser fails the build citing C-3.5

Given `make up` is run on WSL Ubuntu with no Bybit credentials
When the compose stack starts
Then api, postgres, questdb, prometheus, grafana and minio all reach healthy within 120s and `curl localhost:8000/healthz` returns 200

Given docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml is edited
When `pnpm generate` has not been re-run
Then the generated-code staleness check fails with a non-empty diff
```

## Technical notes / design
Layout is fixed by `20-architecture.md` §5 and must be reproduced exactly (paths are cited by CODEOWNERS, import-linter contracts and later tickets). JS: pnpm workspaces + Turborepo; Python: `uv` + Hatch, single `services/api/pyproject.toml`. A `Makefile` is the human front-end (`make dev|test|gen|up`) delegating to pnpm/uv so there is one entry point per `20-architecture.md` §5 Tooling. Package names are `@candleviewer/<name>` per `AGENTS.md` §4 filters. All TS projects use `strict: true`; Python uses `mypy --strict`. No package may declare a dependency on an app (C-3.5).

## Test plan
Each child ticket carries its own plan; epic-level: a **clean-clone bootstrap matrix** (fresh WSL Ubuntu container, fresh Windows+WSL dev box) executed by QA (Q02), plus the toolchain regression pack (Q03) that asserts every Constitution §9 gate is runnable locally with the same command CI will use.

## Security notes
Supply-chain is the epic's dominant threat (STRIDE model in X01): dependency confusion, malicious postinstall scripts, lockfile tampering, leaked secrets in `.env`, and container images pulled by mutable tag. Controls: frozen lockfiles, `pnpm` `ignore-scripts` review, pinned image digests in compose, license allowlist (§9 #14), gitleaks baseline, `.env.example` only — never a real `.env` committed. Data classification: no production data touched; compose volumes are local-only and must bind to `127.0.0.1` (C-2 trust boundary B2).

## Accessibility notes
No user-facing screens are introduced. The epic wires the `a11y` tooling seams (axe-core devDependency, Storybook a11y addon hook point in `packages/ui`) consumed by E05/E03. D01 covers the token-pipeline handoff contract.

## Performance notes
No runtime budget from `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` applies yet. Toolchain budgets: `pnpm verify` ≤10 min cold / ≤3 min warm (Turbo cache) on reference hardware (§3.1); `make up` ≤120 s to all-healthy. The chart-engine `bench` task must exist (empty baseline) so E06 can land numbers without re-plumbing.

## Observability
`/healthz` and `/readyz` stubs in `services/api` returning static payloads plus a `build-info` field (git sha, version) — E04 fills in real checks. Compose ships prometheus scraping `api:/metrics` (stub registry) so E04 has a target on day one.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All child tickets Done or explicitly descoped with a recorded disposition.
- [ ] `pnpm verify` and `uv run pytest` green on a clean clone; coverage gates configured at §9 thresholds (may report 100% on empty packages — the *gate must exist*).
- [ ] `AGENTS.md` §4 corrected in the same PR wherever a real script name deviates; `check-agents-commands.mjs` green.
- [ ] ADR-0016 merged.
- [ ] `20-architecture.md` §5 updated if the shipped layout diverged.
- [ ] STRIDE model (X01) complete, findings triaged; Security engineer sign-off.
- [ ] QA epic-level sign-off (Q01–Q03) recorded.
- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review: clean clone → `pnpm verify` → `make up` → healthy stack.
- [ ] Retro note filed.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by: E01` — CODEOWNERS, PR/issue templates, branch protection and the Constitution ratification must exist before the tree they own is created. Downstream: E03, E04, E05, E06, E07, E08 all consume this scaffold.

## Branch
`feat/monorepo-scaffold-*` per child ticket; epic itself has no branch. PR size: each child ≤400 LOC diff excluding lockfiles and generated output (C-4.8); lockfile-only churn declared in the PR body.

## References
- docs/plan/20-architecture.md#5-monorepo-layout
- docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md §4.2, §11.1, §12
- /CONSTITUTION.md §3, §9
- /AGENTS.md §4
- docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md, docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md

## Dependency graph of children
```mermaid
flowchart TD
    K01[K01 Spike tooling ADR] --> T01[T01 pnpm+Turbo root]
    K01 --> T02[T02 Python uv workspace]
    T01 --> T03[T03 TS package skeletons]
    T01 --> T07[T07 commitlint/husky/editorconfig]
    T03 --> T04[T04 apps/web + apps/desktop]
    T02 --> T05[T05 services/api skeleton M1-M24]
    T05 --> T06[T06 import-linter + dep-cruiser]
    T03 --> T06
    T05 --> T08[T08 docker compose + Makefile]
    T03 --> T09[T09 protocol codegen + staleness]
    T05 --> T09
    T03 --> T10[T10 coverage + verify gates]
    T05 --> T10
    T06 --> T11[T11 ADR-0016 + AGENTS reconcile]
    T09 --> T11
    D01[D01 token pipeline handoff] --> T03
    T10 --> Q01[Q01 scaffold test plan]
    T08 --> Q02[Q02 clean-clone charter]
    T10 --> Q03[Q03 toolchain regression pack]
    T01 --> X01[X01 STRIDE supply chain]
    X01 --> X02[X02 SAST/secrets/license baseline]
```

## Estimate reconciliation (2026-09-14)
The locked roadmap allocates **42 pts** to E02 (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §3 epic register, line 102; §4.2 R0 scope table, line 185). An earlier backlog draft summed to 64 pts (+52%), far outside the ±15% tolerance. **Resolution: the roadmap is authoritative and unchanged; the backlog was re-estimated down to 42 pts.** Every child ticket carries an "Estimate reconciliation" note recording its old and new figure and the rationale (scaffolding work is overwhelmingly generator-driven: `pnpm create`, `uv init`, Turborepo/Vitest presets, Electron Forge and upstream compose templates; the original numbers priced it as bespoke implementation).

Current roll-up (must stay equal to the roadmap figure — any change requires a roadmap PR, not a silent backlog edit):

| Kind | Tickets | Pts |
|---|---|---|
| Spike | K01 | 2 |
| Task (engineering) | T01–T10 | 27 |
| Task (docs) | T11–T12 | 3 |
| Design | D01 | 2 |
| QA | Q01–Q03 | 4 |
| Security | X01–X02 | 4 |
| **Total** | **19** | **42** |

Guard: if in-sprint discovery pushes the true size above 48 pts (42 + 15%), the disposition is to **descope T12 (onboarding docs) and Q02 (second-machine exploratory charter) into R0 sprint S03/E03**, not to overrun S02 — both are P2 and neither gates E03/E05/E06/E07/E08.

## Schedule risk & buffer
E02 is the single highest-fan-out node in the roadmap: `E01 → E02 → {E03, E05, E06, E07, E08}` (§11.1) and it opens the critical path `E02 → E06 → E11 → E12 → E18 → E26 → E38 → E44 → E46 → GA` (§12). It starts in **Sprint 01 (2026-09-25)**, the same sprint as its blocker E01, so an E01 slip propagates with no natural slack. This is accepted, with the following explicit mitigations rather than implicit optimism:

1. **Parallel start, not serial.** `E02-K01` (tooling spike) and `E02-D01` (token-handoff contract) are deliberately **not** blocked on E01 — they produce decision documents, not merges into a protected `main`, so they proceed from day 1 of S01 while E01 ratifies the constitution and branch protection.
2. **E01 hard-gate is narrow.** Only `E02-T01` takes the E01 dependency, and only for `CONSTITUTION.md` §3 (module edge table) + CODEOWNERS paths. If E01 slips past S01 day 3, T01 proceeds against the **draft** §3 table on a feature branch; the import-linter contracts in T06 are re-verified against the ratified text before the epic's DoD is claimed.
3. **Named slack in S02.** The S02 tail (`T11`, `T12`, `Q02`, `Q03`, `X02` — 7 pts, all P1/P2, none on the critical path) is the epic's buffer. If S01 delivery slips, these absorb the slip inside E02 rather than pushing the S02 exit date or E06's S02 start.
4. **Downstream unblock order.** Ticket completion is sequenced so the highest-fan-out artefacts land first: `T01/T03` (packages exist) unblocks E05/E06 mid-S01; `T02/T05` unblocks E07/E08; `T06/T10` (gates) unblocks E03. E03/E05/E06 do **not** wait for the whole epic to close.
5. **Tracking.** Logged as a schedule-risk item against **R5 Scope** in `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md`; reviewed at the S01 mid-sprint checkpoint. Trigger: if `E02-T01` is not merged by S01 day 5, escalate at once and cut T12/Q02 per the guard above.


## Agent guidance

How to pick up work in this epic when multiple agents are running in parallel:

**Dependency order.** Work tickets in `blocked_by` order; a ticket is not pickable until every key in its `blocked_by` list is Done. Design (`-D*`) and spike (`-K*`) tickets generally gate the technical (`-T*`) and story (`-S*`) tickets that consume their output — check each ticket's `blocked_by` field, do not assume numeric order implies dependency order.

**Parallel lanes.** Tickets with disjoint `component` values and no shared `blocked_by` edge can run concurrently: backend (`api`/`data-feeds`) tickets, frontend (`web`) tickets and design (`-D*`) tickets form separate lanes once their own upstream design/contract tickets are Done. QA (`-Q*`) and security (`-X*`) tickets typically depend on the corresponding `-S*`/`-T*` ticket being Done, so they are the last lane per feature slice, not a separate epic-wide phase.

**Shared interfaces to agree first.** Before two agents touch the same contract (API/WS schema, DB table, or statechart) concurrently, the one opening the PR first must land the contract change (OpenAPI/WS schema/migration) and regenerate `packages/protocol`; the second agent rebases on it rather than proposing a second incompatible shape. Statechart JSON under `machines/` is single-owner per PR — check open PRs touching the same `machines/<name>.machine.json` before starting a `statechart`-labelled ticket.

**This epic's tickets:**

- `E02-T01` (Task, infra) — blocked_by: E01, E02-K01
- `E02-T02` (Task, infra) — blocked_by: E02-K01

title: Spike: pnpm+Turborepo vs Nx and uv vs Poetry for the CandleViewer monorepo
body:
## Context
`20-architecture.md` §5 states the intended tooling as "pnpm workspaces + Turborepo for JS; `uv` + Hatch for Python", and `30-release-roadmap.md` §4.2 phrases the Python side as "uv/poetry" — i.e. the JS choice is strongly indicated but the Python packaging/lock tool is **not yet decided**, and neither choice has been measured against this repo's actual gate set (`CONSTITUTION.md` §9: 20 required checks, ≤15 min commit→dev per R0 exit criterion 2). Because every subsequent ticket in E02 and all of E03's workflow files hard-code these tools, the decision must be closed in the first days of S01, timeboxed, before T01/T02 start.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Timebox: **3 working days**, 1 engineer (Architect-supervised), spike branch `spike/monorepo-tooling`.
- Build a throwaway prototype with 2 TS packages + 1 app + 1 Python service that exercises: install from lockfile, lint, typecheck, unit test with coverage, build, and a cross-package task dependency, under (a) pnpm+Turborepo, (b) pnpm+Nx.
- Python side: same skeleton under (a) `uv` + Hatch, (b) Poetry — measuring lock/install time, mypy-strict integration, editable installs for `services/api`, and CI cache friendliness.
- Measure on the reference hardware of `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §3.1: cold install, warm install, cold full-gate, warm (cached) full-gate, cache hit-rate on a one-file change.
- Produce a comparison table and **ADR-0016** (drafted here, merged in E02-T11).

## Out of scope
- Production-shippable code (per DoR §5.1, this spike's output is throwaway).
- CI workflow authoring (E03).
- Bundler choice for `apps/web` (Vite is locked by `20-architecture.md` §5) and Electron builder choice (locked: `electron-builder.yml`).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Given the 3-day timebox
When the spike completes
Then a comparison table with cold/warm install and gate timings for all four candidate combinations is recorded on the ticket

Given the measured numbers
When the Architect reviews
Then ADR-0016 is drafted with an explicit decision and a stated reversal cost per option

Given a candidate whose warm full-gate exceeds 5 minutes on reference hardware
When the decision is made
Then that candidate is rejected outright, because R0 exit criterion 2 requires commit→dev ≤15 min including container build and five scanners

Given the spike cannot answer the Python question within the timebox
When the timebox expires
Then ADR-0016 records "defer with uv as the provisional default" (DoR §5.2 permits a defer-ADR) and a follow-up Task is filed rather than silently extending
```

## Technical notes / design
The prototype must include one deliberately awkward case each tool must handle: a TS package consumed by both another package and an app (task-graph fan-in), and a Python package with a generated module (`packages/protocol` analogue) whose staleness must be detectable. Record Turbo/Nx remote-cache configurability (E03 will want it) and whether `uv`'s resolver handles the pinned stack of `20-architecture.md` §2.1 (FastAPI/Starlette/uvicorn+uvloop, numpy, SQLAlchemy 2.0, pydantic v2, alembic, duckdb, questdb client).

## Test plan
N/A as production tests. Evidence required: timing runs are the median of 5, scripted (`spike/bench.sh`) and attached, not hand-timed; each candidate's gate must actually run ruff/mypy/pytest/eslint/tsc/vitest, not stubs.

## Security notes
While evaluating, record each tool's lifecycle-script behaviour (`pnpm` `ignore-scripts`, Poetry/uv build isolation) and lockfile integrity guarantees — this feeds the supply-chain STRIDE model in E02-X01. Do not add any registry credentials to the spike branch.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — no UI surface.

## Performance notes
Toolchain-only budgets stated above (cold gate ≤10 min, warm ≤5 min, install-from-lock ≤3 min cold).

## Observability
N/A. Timing output is written to `spike/results.json` and pasted into the ticket.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Questions answered with recorded benchmark evidence (median of 5, script attached).
- [ ] ADR-0016 drafted in `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0018-monorepo-tooling.md` (merged by E02-T11).
- [ ] Follow-up tickets exist for the chosen path (T01/T02 updated with the decision).
- [ ] Spike branch marked throwaway and left unmerged.
- [ ] Findings presented at Sprint Review.
- [ ] `32-risk-register.md` updated if a new toolchain risk surfaced.

## Dependencies
Blocked by E01 (branching/spike-branch conventions and the ADR process must be ratified first). Blocks E02-T01 and E02-T02.

## Branch
`spike/monorepo-tooling` — not merged. PR: none (findings posted on the ticket + ADR PR in T11).

## References
- docs/plan/20-architecture.md#5-monorepo-layout
- docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md §4.2, §4.3 exit criterion 2
- /CONSTITUTION.md §9
- docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md §5

## Estimate reconciliation (2026-09-14)
Rebaselined from 3 to 2 pts as part of the epic-level reconciliation to the roadmap-locked **42 pts** for E02 (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §3 line 102 and §4.2 line 185). The roadmap allocation is authoritative and was not changed; the backlog was re-estimated. Scope in this ticket is unchanged — the earlier number double-counted generator/boilerplate effort that `pnpm create`, `uv init`, Turborepo presets and the compose templates supply for free. If delivery shows the new figure is wrong, raise it at sprint review and re-plan the epic; do **not** silently re-inflate the ticket.

## Schedule risk & buffer
Deliberately **not** blocked on E01: this ticket produces a decision/handoff document rather than a merge into a protected `main`, so it starts on day 1 of Sprint 01 in parallel with E01's ratification. This removes the zero-slack serial start flagged against E02, the roadmap's highest-fan-out epic (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §11.1, §12). Its output must be re-checked against the ratified `CONSTITUTION.md` §3 text before `E02-T06` claims Done.


## Agent execution brief

**Read first**
1. docs/plan/20-architecture.md#5-monorepo-layout
2. docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md §4.2, §4.3 exit criterion 2
3. /CONSTITUTION.md §9
4. docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md §5

**Repo paths to create/modify**
- `infra/`
- `.github/workflows/`
- `tests/` — mirrored unit/integration test paths for the module(s) above

**Interfaces you must not break**
- None beyond what's listed in References.

**Commands**
- `pnpm lint`
- `pnpm verify`

**Branch & PR**
- Branch: `spike/monorepo-tooling`
- PR title: "E02-K01: Spike: pnpm+Turborepo vs Nx and uv vs Poetry for the CandleViewer monorepo"
- PR description includes: `Closes #<issue>`
- Required reviewers (CODEOWNERS): @CandleViewer/devsecops
- Labels: type/spike, area/backend-platform, area/frontend-platform, priority/p0

**Done means**
- Questions answered with recorded benchmark evidence (median of 5, script attached).
- ADR-0016 drafted in `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0018-monorepo-tooling.md` (merged by E02-T11).
- Follow-up tickets exist for the chosen path (T01/T02 updated with the decision).
- Spike branch marked throwaway and left unmerged.
- Findings presented at Sprint Review.
- `32-risk-register.md` updated if a new toolchain risk surfaced.

**Do NOT**
- Production-shippable code (per DoR §5.1, this spike's output is throwaway).
- CI workflow authoring (E03).
- Bundler choice for `apps/web` (Vite is locked by `20-architecture.md` §5) and Electron builder choice (locked: `electron-builder.yml`).

**If blocked**
- Comment on this ticket's GitHub issue naming the exact blocking condition (missing contract, failing upstream gate, ambiguous acceptance criterion) and the ticket key it depends on. Move the issue's Status to **Blocked**. Do not silently work around a failing gate, widen scope, or guess at an undocumented contract — stop and wait for the blocker to clear.

## Agent-delivery adaptations (owner decision 2026-09-25)
Delivery is executed by parallel AI agents with a single human owner (`@basiltt`). Where this ticket's text assumes the original 15-person org, apply these substitutions — they are binding and satisfy the corresponding DoR/DoD items:
- **Architect / CDO / Security-engineer sign-off or countersignature** → the **owner's** `approved` comment on this issue, or owner merge of the PR. No other human role exists. Do not block on a missing countersignature — proceed and record "owner approval pending" in the PR.
- **Design tooling**: *Figma* → **Penpot** (`docs/design/README.md`); frames on a page named after this ticket; exports via `docs/design/_tools/penpot_export.py`. Bind only to semantic tokens in `packages/ui/tokens/`.
- **Moderated usability / participant sessions** → a documented **heuristic evaluation** (Nielsen + the trading-specific heuristics in `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`), a written session protocol ready for the owner to run later, and an **owner walkthrough** checklist posted on the issue. Never fabricate participants, timings or quotes; label all findings `(heuristic)`.
- **CVD / contrast validation** → computed programmatically (WCAG contrast matrix over the token JSON; CVD simulation via a documented script), attached as artefacts.
- **Spikes**: findings go to `docs/plan/spikes/<KEY>.md` via a normal PR (branch `spike/<epic>-<slug>`); any ADR named by the spike uses the **next free number** in `docs/plan/27-adrs/` (ADR-0001…0016 are taken).
- **Dependencies**: `blocked_by` now lists the concrete prerequisite tickets (not whole epics). Start when those are **merged** (In Test or Done).
- Anything that genuinely needs a human that is not the owner (external pen-test vendor, legal) stays as-is and is flagged `needs-owner` on the issue.

title: Create root pnpm workspace, Turborepo task graph and shared config package
body:
## Context
The repository has no JS workspace at all. Every frontend and engine ticket from R0 onward (`E05` design system, `E06` engine spike, `E10` shell, `E11` engine core) needs a workspace root with a task graph whose task **names** match `AGENTS.md` §4 exactly — that file is the single place command names are enumerated, and `generated-code-check` (Constitution §9 #19) fails the build when the documented set and the real task graph diverge.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `/package.json` (private, packageManager pinned), `/pnpm-workspace.yaml` covering `apps/*`, `packages/*`.
- `/turbo.json` defining pipelines with correct `dependsOn` edges and cache inputs/outputs for: `lint`, `lint:fix`, `format`, `typecheck`, `test`, `test:cov`, `build`, `size`, `generate`, `verify`.
- `packages/config`: shared **ESLint flat config** (`eslint.config.mjs`), Prettier config, `tsconfig.base.json` (+ `tsconfig.node.json`, `tsconfig.dom.json`), Vitest preset, and a `no-restricted-imports` rule set stub consumed by E02-T06.

```gherkin
When `pnpm verify` runs

Given AGENTS.md §4 documents a task `pnpm size`
When that task is removed from turbo.json
Then `node scripts/check-agents-commands.mjs` exits non-zero naming the missing task
```

```gherkin

When `pnpm build` runs at the root
Then each package builds in topological order and emits its declared exports with type declarations

Given packages/chart-engine
When a source file imports React or calls fetch
Then the lint rule enforcing C-2.16 fails the build with a message citing C-2.16

Given packages/protocol/src/generated

```

title: Scaffold apps/web (Vite+React+TS) and apps/desktop (Electron shell) skeletons
body:
## Context
`20-architecture.md` §5 defines `apps/web` (React SPA, Vite, feature-sliced `src/features/`, `src/lib/{ws,state,auth}`, `e2e/`) and `apps/desktop` (Electron shell, `src/main`, `src/preload`, `e2e/`, `electron-builder.yml`) with **no business logic** in the shell (C-3.5). E10 builds the real routing tree, RBAC guards and hardened Electron main; this Task delivers only the bootable skeletons plus the security switches asserted by a test, because R0 exit criterion 9 requires the Electron shell to "start with the hardened security switches enabled (verified by an automated assertion, not by inspection)" and it is far cheaper to make that assertion true from the first commit than to retro-fit it.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `apps/web`: Vite + React 18 + TS app booting to a single placeholder route; directory skeleton `src/{routes,features,lib/ws,lib/state,lib/auth}` with README stubs stating ownership; Vitest component test setup; `e2e/` with Playwright configured and one smoke spec; dependencies on `@candleviewer/{ui,protocol,chart-engine}` declared.
- `apps/desktop`: Electron main + context-isolated preload loading the web build; `electron-builder.yml`; `e2e/` with Playwright-Electron and a main-window smoke spec.
- Hardened defaults asserted in code and test: `contextIsolation: true`, `nodeIntegration: false`, `sandbox: true`, `webSecurity: true`, strict CSP header/meta, `window.open` denied via `setWindowOpenHandler`, `will-navigate` restricted to the app origin, and an explicit IPC channel allow-list in preload (empty at this stage).
- `apps/web` size-limit budget entry wired to the `size` task (Constitution §9 #15; budget #9 of `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`: ≤8 MB gzipped initial Electron renderer).

## Out of scope
- Route tree per `12-sitemap.md`, auth/RBAC guards, env badge, global shortcut registry, auto-update, crash reporting — all **E10**.
- Any chart rendering, WS client implementation, or state stores beyond empty directories.
- GPU flag tuning — depends on E06's findings and lands in E10.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Given a built web bundle
When `pnpm --filter @candleviewer/desktop dev` launches Electron
Then the main window loads the app and the Playwright-Electron smoke spec passes

Given the Electron main process
When the hardening assertion test runs
Then it reads the actual BrowserWindow webPreferences at runtime and fails if any of contextIsolation, sandbox or webSecurity is false or nodeIntegration is true

Given the renderer
When it attempts window.open to an external URL
Then the request is denied by setWindowOpenHandler and an audit-able log line is emitted

Given apps/web
When the initial bundle exceeds 8MB gzipped or regresses more than 5% versus main
Then the `size` task fails, per Constitution §9 #15

Given apps/web
When axe-core runs against the placeholder route via @axe-core/playwright
Then zero serious or critical violations are reported
```

## Technical notes / design
The preload exposes exactly one namespaced object (`window.cv`) built from an explicit allow-list array; adding a channel later requires editing that array, which is code-owned by the security engineer (trust boundary B4, `20-architecture.md` §2.2). CSP is `default-src 'self'; connect-src 'self' ws: wss:; img-src 'self' data:; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'` — `'unsafe-inline'` for styles only, with a follow-up ticket to move to nonces once the design system's styling approach is fixed in E05. The shell must keep all shell-specific code behind a `ShellPort` abstraction because ADR-0011 (Electron vs Tauri) is `proposed`, not decided (`20-architecture.md` note; E06 closes it).

## Test plan
- Unit (Vitest): preload allow-list builder rejects a channel not in the list; CSP string builder snapshot.
- Integration: Electron hardening assertion test reading live `webPreferences`.
- E2E: Playwright web smoke (app boots, placeholder route renders) and Playwright-Electron main-window smoke — these become the seeds of the `e2e-smoke` gate (Constitution §9 #8).
- a11y: `@axe-core/playwright` on the placeholder route.
- Perf: `size` budget check.

body:
## Context

## Scope / Deliverables
- `services/api/candleviewer/` package with one subpackage per module M1–M24 at the exact paths of `CONSTITUTION.md` §3, each following the convention of `20-architecture.md` §3: `__init__.py` exporting only the public interface, `service.py` (lifecycle), `models.py` (pydantic v2 domain types), `errors.py`.
- **M1 `config` implemented**: `settings.py` using `pydantic-settings` with env layering, `Environment` enum (`live`|`demo`|`testnet`), datastore DSNs (Postgres, QuestDB, DuckDB/Parquet root, MinIO), feature-flag defaults, and a `CV_FEED` switch (`live`|`synthetic`) per `20-architecture.md` §5 note on the synthetic feed.
- `app.py` composition root building `AppContext` (settings, bus, storage clients, key vault, metric registry, clock guard, module instances) — all fields present and typed, with fakes/None-objects where the owning epic has not landed; module supervisor with the documented start/stop ordering hook (`20-architecture.md` §6.2).
- FastAPI application factory exposing `/healthz`, `/readyz` and a build-info payload (git sha, version, environment) — static responses; E04 replaces them with real probes.
- `services/api/candleviewer/migrations/` alembic skeleton directory (empty revision tree, single-head check runnable) — content is E07's.

## Out of scope
- Any module's real logic (exchange, ingestion, book, bars, orderflow, oms, rules, paper, recorder, replay, accounts, risk, auth, audit, journal, admin, api routers, ws gateway, storage implementations, observability wiring) — owned by later epics.
- import-linter contract files (E02-T06). Docker packaging (E02-T08).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Given the module tree
When a reviewer compares it to CONSTITUTION.md §3
Then all 24 module paths exist with the exact names M1..M24 map to, and a test asserts this programmatically against a checked-in manifest

Given CV_ENV=demo and a .env file
When the settings object loads
Then the Environment enum resolves to demo and an invalid value raises a pydantic ValidationError naming the allowed values

Given the composition root
When `create_app()` is called in a unit test with fake storage clients
Then it constructs without touching Postgres, QuestDB or the network, and GET /healthz returns 200 with a build-info body containing gitSha, version and environment

Given a module's __init__.py
When it re-exports an internal implementation symbol not listed in its public interface manifest
Then the public-surface test fails, citing the §3 convention
```

## Technical notes / design
`AppContext` is a frozen dataclass; modules receive it (or narrower protocols) by constructor injection — never a global. The supervisor start order follows the dependency numbering of §3 (config → secrets → storage → bus → exchange → ingestion → …) and shutdown is the reverse, with a bounded drain timeout. Settings must never log their own values: `__repr__` redacts any field whose name matches `(key|secret|token|password|dsn)` — an early instance of E04's redaction filter requirement. `Environment` is used later by C-1 guardrails (trading mode refuses to start if a stored key has withdrawal enabled, `20-architecture.md` §2.2 B3) so the enum lives in M1, not in a trading module.

- Unit: module-manifest test (24 paths, public-surface check); settings validation (valid/invalid env, missing required DSN, env-file layering precedence); redacting `__repr__`; `create_app()` with fakes; `/healthz` and `/readyz` response schema.

- Integration: none (E02-T08 runs the app inside compose).

The redacting `__repr__` and the ban on logging settings are the primary controls here (Information Disclosure). M2 `secrets` is created as an empty module but its import restriction (C-3.2: importable only by M4 and M21) must already be encoded in the manifest so T06 can enforce it. No real credentials are introduced; `.env.example` only. `/healthz` and `/readyz` must not leak versions of datastores or internal hostnames to an unauthenticated caller — build-info is limited to git sha, semver and environment name.

title: Encode module boundaries as import-linter and dependency-cruiser contracts
body:
## Context
`CONSTITUTION.md` C-3.1 ("dependencies flow one way … cycles are forbidden"), C-3.2 (M2 `secrets` importable only by M4 and M21, "Enforced by CI"), C-3.3 (M19 `audit` write-only except M21/M23 read paths), C-3.5 (`apps/web` never imports another app; `packages/*` never import `apps/*`) and C-2.16 (chart-engine framework-free) are stated as CI-enforced invariants, and §9 #18 names the blocking check: "`architecture` — `import-linter` module-boundary contracts (§3) + `dependency-cruiser` for TS + deep-import ban". None of this exists yet. This Task writes the contracts; E03 wires the job into GitHub Actions.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `services/api/.importlinter` with, at minimum: a **layers** contract encoding the M1→M24 numbering of §3; a **forbidden** contract for C-3.2 (only `exchange.bybit` and `admin` may import `secrets`); a **forbidden** contract for C-3.3 (only `admin` and `api` may import `audit` read APIs); an **independence** contract between sibling engine modules that §3 does not connect; a global no-cycles assertion.
- Per-module `allowed` lists transcribed verbatim from the §3 table into a single machine-readable manifest (`docs/plan/module-contracts.toml` or `services/api/module_contracts.toml`) that both import-linter and the §3 doc-drift test read, so the table and the contracts cannot diverge.
- `.dependency-cruiser.js` at the root: `packages/* -/-> apps/*`, `apps/web -/-> apps/desktop` (and reverse), deep-import ban (only package `exports` entry points), `packages/chart-engine -/-> react|react-dom` and no `fetch`/`XMLHttpRequest`/`bybit` identifiers (C-2.16, C-2.2), `packages/protocol` may not import `packages/ui` or `apps/*`.
- ESLint `no-restricted-imports` mirror for fast editor feedback (C-3.5 note: "enforced by `no-restricted-imports` and by `import-linter` on the Python side").
- A **drift test** asserting the manifest matches the §3 table in `CONSTITUTION.md` (parses the markdown table) — so amending §3 without amending the contracts fails CI, and vice versa.
- `make arch` / `pnpm arch` task running both linters; added to `verify` and documented in `AGENTS.md` §4.

## Out of scope
- The GitHub Actions `architecture` job definition (E03).
- Adding new modules or edges (requires an ADR per C-3.4).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Given the contracts are in place
When `make arch` runs on the clean scaffold
Then both import-linter and dependency-cruiser exit 0 with every contract reported as kept

Given a deliberate violation adding `from candleviewer.secrets import KeyVault` to candleviewer/oms/service.py
When `make arch` runs
Then it exits non-zero naming the C-3.2 contract and the offending import chain

Given a deliberate violation adding `import React from "react"` to packages/chart-engine/src/core/index.ts
When `make arch` runs
Then dependency-cruiser fails citing C-2.16

Given a deliberate deep import `@candleviewer/ui/src/primitives/Button` from apps/web
When `make arch` runs
Then the deep-import ban fails the build

Given the M14 row of CONSTITUTION.md §3 is edited to add a dependency
When the drift test runs without a matching manifest change
Then the test fails, stating that §3 and module_contracts.toml disagree
```

## Technical notes / design
The manifest is the single source of truth *for machines*; `CONSTITUTION.md` §3 remains the source for *humans*, and the drift test binds them (this mirrors C-16.5: never duplicate an owned list without a mechanical check). Import-linter layers alone cannot express C-3.2/C-3.3 — use additional `forbidden` contracts with `ignore_imports` empty (no exceptions). Cycle detection: `import-linter`'s independence contracts plus a `grimp`-based no-cycles test. For TS, dependency-cruiser's `forbidden` rules carry a `comment` field citing the exact Constitution rule id so failures are self-explanatory. Every violation message must name the rule id — reviewers cite rule ids in PRs (Constitution preamble).

## Test plan
- Unit: the drift test (markdown table parser) with fixtures for matching, added-edge and removed-edge cases.
- Integration: a **negative-test suite** that, for each of the five acceptance violations, applies a patch in a temp copy of the tree, runs `make arch`, asserts non-zero exit and the expected rule id in stderr, then restores. This is the only way to prove the gate is real rather than merely configured.
- Coverage: the drift-test helper counts toward the backend threshold.

## Security notes
This Task *is* a security control: C-3.2 keeps the envelope-encryption/key-vault module (M2 `secrets`) unreachable from business logic, which is the structural mitigation for key-leakage threats in `04-security-program.md`; C-3.3 keeps the audit log append-only from every module's perspective, protecting non-repudiation. A weakened or `ignore_imports`-ridden contract is itself a security finding — the contract files must be added to `.github/CODEOWNERS` under the security engineer (coordinated with E01). Requires Security engineer review before Done.

N/A — build-time static analysis, no UI surface.

`make arch` must complete in ≤60 s on the full tree so it can live inside `verify` and the ≤15 min pipeline (R0 exit criterion 2). Cache dependency-cruiser results per Turbo inputs.

Both linters emit machine-readable reports (`arch-report.json`) uploaded as a CI artefact by E03, giving a trend of contract count over time.

title: Add commitlint, husky, lint-staged and .editorconfig with conventional-commit enforcement
body:
## Context
`00-planning-brief.md` §SDLC requires conventional commits, and `CONSTITUTION.md` §9 #20 (`pr-metadata`) gates on "Conventional-commit title, `Closes #N` present, branch-name pattern, diff-size policy (C-4.8)". Release automation in `07-release-and-prr.md` derives the changelog and semver bump from commit types, so a single non-conforming commit on `main` corrupts a release note. Catching this locally (husky) is far cheaper than catching it in the merge queue.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `commitlint.config.cjs` extending `@commitlint/config-conventional`, with the scope allow-list derived from the component values used by the board (`chart-engine`, `data-feeds`, `indicators`, `drawing-tools`, `alerts`, `backtesting`, `scripting`, `web`, `api`, `auth`, `collaboration`, `infra`, `docs`) plus package names.
- husky hooks: `commit-msg` (commitlint), `pre-commit` (lint-staged: eslint --fix + prettier on staged JS/TS, ruff --fix + black on staged Python), `pre-push` (typecheck on changed projects only, with an escape hatch documented for emergencies).
- `lint-staged` config in the root `package.json`.
- `/.editorconfig`: UTF-8, LF, final newline, trim trailing whitespace, 2-space for JS/TS/JSON/YAML/MD, 4-space for Python, `max_line_length` matching Ruff/Black (88) and Prettier (100 for TS).
- `scripts/check-branch-name.mjs` validating `feat/…`, `fix/…`, `chore/…`, `design/…`, `spike/…` per `01-sdlc-and-branching.md`, wired into `pre-push` and reusable by E03's `pr-metadata` job.

## Out of scope
- The GitHub Actions `pr-metadata` job and PR template (E01/E03).
- release-please / changelog automation (E03).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Given a commit message "fixed stuff"
When the commit-msg hook runs
Then the commit is rejected with a message showing the conventional-commit format and the allowed scopes

Given a commit message "feat(chart-engine): add SDF glyph atlas"
When the commit-msg hook runs
Then the commit is accepted

Given staged TypeScript with formatting errors and staged Python with import-order errors
When the pre-commit hook runs
Then both are auto-fixed and re-staged, and the commit proceeds
```

title: Author docker compose stack for WSL Ubuntu (api, postgres, questdb, prometheus, grafana, minio)
body:
## Context
`30-release-roadmap.md` §4.2 puts "Docker Compose for WSL Ubuntu (api, postgres, questdb, grafana, prometheus, minio-for-parquet)" inside E02, and `20-architecture.md` §5 places it at `infra/compose/` with `.dev`/`.vps` overrides and `.env.example`, started by `make up`. Three separate consumers depend on it: engineers (`make up` with `CV_FEED=synthetic` so they can work without Bybit credentials), the `integration` CI gate ("Backend + Postgres + QuestDB in docker compose, driven by recorded Bybit fixtures; **no network egress**", Constitution §9 #7), and E04's observability work (Prometheus must already be scraping the api target). Trust boundary B2 (`20-architecture.md` §2.2) requires services to bind `127.0.0.1`/WSL-internal only — never `0.0.0.0`, because of the WSL portproxy leak risk.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml` + `docker-compose.dev.yml` + `docker-compose.vps.yml` overrides + `.env.example` (no real secrets).
- Services with pinned image **digests**: postgres 16, questdb 8.x, prometheus 2.x, grafana 11, minio (Parquet cold-tier stand-in), and `api` built from `infra/images/Dockerfile.api` (multi-stage, non-root user, no dev deps in the runtime layer).
- Named volumes for postgres data, questdb data, minio data, grafana data; documented reset path.
- Healthchecks for every service; `depends_on: condition: service_healthy` so `make up` is deterministic.
- Port bindings **explicitly** `127.0.0.1:<port>:<port>` for every published port (B2); an internal network `cv-internal`.
- `infra/prometheus/prometheus.yml` scraping `api:8000/metrics` (target exists thanks to E02-T05); `infra/grafana/` provisioning stubs (datasource only — dashboards are E04).
- `infra/scripts/bootstrap.sh` (create DBs/buckets, apply nothing else) and `infra/scripts/healthcheck.sh` used by `make up` to wait for all-healthy.
- `make up`, `make down`, `make reset` documented in `AGENTS.md` §4.

## Out of scope
- Grafana dashboards, alert rules, Alertmanager routing, structlog redaction — **E04**.
- QuestDB tuning, DDL, retention jobs, Parquet layout — **E07**.
- CI job that starts the stack — **E03** (this Task only guarantees it is startable and scriptable).
- Any VPS provisioning or deployment.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Given a WSL Ubuntu host with Docker and no Bybit credentials
When `make up` runs
Then all six services reach healthy within 120 seconds and `make up` exits 0

Given the stack is healthy
When `curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/healthz` and `curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/readyz` are called
Then both return 200 and readyz lists its (currently empty) checks array

Given the compose files
When a reviewer greps for port bindings
Then every published port is bound to 127.0.0.1 and none to 0.0.0.0, asserted by a test script in infra/scripts

Given CV_FEED=synthetic
When the api service starts
Then it starts successfully without any exchange credentials present in the environment

Given `make reset`
When it is run after data has been written
Then all named volumes are removed and a subsequent `make up` reaches healthy from a clean state

Given an image tag is used instead of a pinned digest
When the compose lint script runs
Then it fails, citing the supply-chain control from the E02 STRIDE model
```

## Technical notes / design
The `api` image is multi-stage: builder installs with `uv sync --frozen`, runtime copies the venv and application only, runs as UID 10001, read-only root filesystem with explicit writable tmpfs. Compose profiles separate `core` (postgres, questdb, api) from `obs` (prometheus, grafana) and `cold` (minio) so the `integration` gate can start only what it needs and stay fast. Prometheus scrape interval 15 s. MinIO is the local stand-in for the Parquet/object cold tier described in `20-architecture.md` §2.1 C18; the `.vps.yml` override can swap it for a filesystem path. `.env.example` documents every variable M1 `config` reads, with safe defaults and explicit `CHANGE_ME` markers for anything secret-like.

## Test plan
- Integration: `infra/scripts/healthcheck.sh` asserted in a test that runs `make up`, polls health, hits `/healthz`, `/readyz`, `/metrics`, then `make down` — this becomes the seed of Constitution §9 #7's harness.
- Unit/lint: compose lint script tests — (a) any `0.0.0.0` binding fails, (b) any untagged/digest-less image fails, (c) any service missing a healthcheck fails.
- Chaos (light): kill the postgres container and assert the api `/readyz` turns non-ready once E04 adds real probes — recorded as a follow-up assertion, not gated here.
- Coverage: script tests counted under the backend threshold.

## Security notes
Threats (E02-X01 STRIDE): (1) **Exposure** — a `0.0.0.0` binding on WSL is reachable from the LAN via portproxy; mitigated by the loopback-only rule plus the automated grep test (B2). (2) **Supply chain** — mutable image tags allow silent substitution; mitigated by pinned digests plus Trivy in E03 (§9 #13). (3) **Credential leakage** — only `.env.example` is committed, `.env` is gitignored and gitleaks-scanned; default Postgres/Grafana/MinIO credentials must be `CHANGE_ME` and the bootstrap script must refuse to run with them in a non-dev profile. (4) **Container escape surface** — non-root user, read-only rootfs, no `privileged`, no docker socket mount anywhere. Data classification: local development data only; no live account data or API keys are ever placed in this stack (keys are E27's concern and are envelope-encrypted with a KEK held in the host OS keychain, outside WSL — B3).

## Accessibility notes
N/A — infrastructure, no UI surface. (Grafana's own UI is third-party and out of the WCAG scope of `05-accessibility-standard.md`, which covers CandleViewer's own screens.)

## Performance notes
`make up` to all-healthy ≤120 s cold, ≤30 s warm on reference hardware (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §3.1). Resource limits are declared per service so a laptop dev box is not starved; the sizing basis for the eventual VPS is §10.2 of the same doc and is **not** applied here.

## Observability
Prometheus scrapes `api:8000/metrics`; Grafana is provisioned with the Prometheus datasource only. Compose logs use the `json-file` driver with rotation (`max-size=10m`, `max-file=3`) so a long soak cannot fill a dev disk — relevant to the 24 h ingestion soak in R0 exit criterion 5.

title: Build packages/protocol code generation from OpenAPI + WS schema with staleness gate
body:
## Context
`CONSTITUTION.md` C-6.6 states "`packages/protocol` types are **generated** from the contract" and §9 #19 (`generated-code-check`) blocks merge when regeneration produces a diff. `20-architecture.md` §5 phrases the rule as "`packages/protocol` is generated from `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` and the WS schema — CI fails if the generated output is stale (`make gen && git diff --exit-code`)". The contract documents already exist and are baselines: `22-api-openapi.yaml` (OpenAPI 3.1, base path `/api/v1`, RFC 9457 problem bodies, decimal-string money fields per convention C6, RFC 3339 timestamps per C7) and `23-ws-protocol.md` (envelope with `ch` topic, `s` per-(connection,topic) sequence, message kinds `sub_ok`/`snap`/`delta`/`resync`/`err`, JSON and binary encodings per §3.2/§3.4). Nothing generates from them yet, so every later epic would otherwise hand-write drifting types.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `pnpm generate` pipeline producing `packages/protocol/src/generated/`: TS types for every OpenAPI schema and operation (request/response/problem), and TS types for the WS envelope, every message kind and every topic payload declared in `23-ws-protocol.md` §6 topic catalogue.
- A machine-readable WS schema artefact: extract the topic/message table of `23-ws-protocol.md` into `docs/plan/ws-schema.json` (JSON Schema per message kind and topic) as the generator's input, with a doc-drift test binding it to the markdown (same pattern as E02-T06's §3 manifest).
- Python side: generate pydantic v2 models into `services/api/candleviewer/api/_generated/` (REST schemas) and `services/api/candleviewer/ws/_generated/` (frame schemas) from the same two inputs, so backend and frontend cannot disagree.
- Money/decimal handling per convention C6: money/size/price generate as `string` in TS and `Decimal`-backed types in Python — never `number`/`float`.
- `packages/protocol/src/runtime/`: hand-written binary frame decoder skeleton and `seq`/resync helpers matching `23-ws-protocol.md` §3.4 and §7, with the generated types as their contract.
- Staleness gate: `make gen && git diff --exit-code`, plus a `pnpm generate:check` task documented in `AGENTS.md` §4.
- Generated files carry a do-not-edit header enforced by the guard from E02-T03 and `linguist-generated` in `.gitattributes`.

## Out of scope
- Implementing any endpoint or WS topic (E09, E17 and later epics).
- Changing the contract documents themselves — any needed fix is raised as a contract PR reviewed first (C-6, contract-first).
- MessagePack/binary encoder implementation beyond the decoder skeleton (E17).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Given the committed contracts
When `pnpm generate` runs on a clean tree
Then it exits 0 and `git diff --exit-code` reports no changes

Given a new optional field is added to a schema in docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml
When CI runs generate:check without regeneration
Then the check fails with a diff naming the stale generated file

Given an OpenAPI schema field marked as money (x-decimal or the documented decimal-string convention C6)
When types are generated
Then the TS type is string and the Python type is a Decimal-backed type, asserted by a generator unit test

Given docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md gains a topic row that is absent from ws-schema.json
When the drift test runs
Then it fails, stating that the markdown topic catalogue and the JSON schema disagree

Given a generated file is edited by hand
When lint runs
Then the do-not-edit header guard fails and points the author at `pnpm generate`
```

## Technical notes / design
Generator choice is `openapi-typescript` (types only, no runtime client) for TS and `datamodel-code-generator` for pydantic v2 — both deterministic, both pinned by version so output is byte-stable; a non-deterministic generator would make `generated-code-check` flap and is grounds for rejecting the tool. Generation must be sorted/stable (no timestamps, no absolute paths in output). The WS schema extraction is a one-time authoring job plus a parser test: the markdown table remains human-authoritative, `ws-schema.json` machine-authoritative, and the drift test forbids divergence (C-16.5 pattern). Envelope fields are `t` (type), `ch` (topic), `s` (sequence), `e` (encoding) per §3.1/§3.2 — the envelope type must model `s` as monotonically increasing **per (connection, topic)**, which the resync helper relies on (§3.3, §7).

## Test plan
- Unit (TS): generator output snapshot tests for a representative subset (one paginated list response with `PageMeta` per convention C3, one RFC 9457 `Problem`, one order-mutating request carrying `Idempotency-Key` per C4, one money-bearing schema per C6).
- Unit (Python): pydantic model round-trip tests for the same subset, asserting Decimal preservation (no float coercion) and RFC 3339 parsing with the `_ms` epoch-millis suffix convention (C7).
- Unit: WS envelope decode/encode round trip for each message kind; sequence-gap helper returns a resync decision when `s` jumps.
- Contract: the generated artefacts feed the `contract` gate (§9 #6) — this Task makes that gate possible; a placeholder consumer test asserts the generated type set is non-empty and matches the operation count in the spec.
- Determinism: generate twice in a clean temp dir and assert byte-identical output.
- Coverage: runtime helpers ≥85%; generated files excluded from coverage.

## Security notes
`packages/protocol/src/runtime` decoders parse **untrusted** frames from the network and are therefore a primary attack surface (Tampering/DoS): the decoder must enforce the frame-size limits of `23-ws-protocol.md` §3.6 and reject oversized or malformed frames without allocating proportional memory. Generated code must never embed example credentials from the spec. Flag `src/runtime` as a fuzz target for E03's Schemathesis/fuzz job and for DAST later. No secrets or PII pass through generation.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — type generation, no UI surface.

## Performance notes
`pnpm generate` ≤60 s on the full contract so it stays inside `verify` and the ≤15 min pipeline. Decoder helpers will later be on the hot path for budget #3 (WS tick → screen p95 <100 ms) and budget #6 (≤20 ms backend fan-out add-on) — the skeleton must avoid per-frame allocations and JSON re-parsing, and a microbenchmark placeholder is committed for E17 to extend.

## Observability
Generation emits a manifest (`packages/protocol/generated.manifest.json`) listing input file hashes and generator versions, so a stale-output failure in CI can be diagnosed without local reproduction.

- size-limit configuration for `apps/web` entry points against budget #9 of `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` (≤8 MB gzipped initial renderer) with the +5% regression rule of §9 #15.
- Coverage-baseline file so "no decrease vs `main`" (#3) is checkable locally, plus a documented procedure for the dated, ticket-referenced `omit` list created in E02-T05.
- Negative-test harness (`scripts/gate-negative-tests.mjs`): for each gate, apply a temporary breaking change, assert the gate fails with the expected message, revert.
- Flaky-test plumbing: the `@flaky` pytest marker and Vitest equivalent registered with a quarantine report, per C-9.3 and `03-testing-strategy.md` §14.

## Out of scope
- CI workflow files, coverage upload/publishing, PR annotations (E03).
- Writing real tests for real features (owning epics).
- The `engine-bench` 5% gate logic (E06 supplies the baseline; E02-T03 supplied the harness shape).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin

When `pnpm verify` runs
Then it executes exactly the same gate list as the PR required-checks table in CONSTITUTION.md §9, in order, and exits 0

Given a package whose coverage is dropped below its threshold by a temporary change
When the negative-test harness runs
Then that package's gate fails and no other package's gate is affected, proving per-package enforcement

Given apps/web's bundle is inflated past 8MB gzipped by a temporary dependency
When `pnpm size` runs
Then it fails citing budget #9

Given a test marked @flaky
When the suite runs
Then it is quarantined (non-blocking) and listed in the quarantine report with its ticket reference, and an unreferenced @flaky marker fails the run per C-9.3

Given someone lowers a coverage threshold in the same change that would otherwise fail it
When `verify` runs
Then the threshold-guard test fails, citing C-9.4
```

## Technical notes / design
Thresholds are declared once, in each package's own config, and mirrored into a root `quality-gates.json` that the threshold-guard test reads; the guard compares the working tree's thresholds against `main`'s and fails on any decrease not accompanied by an amendment reference. That promise is load-bearing for onboarding (~15 engineers join across R0–R1 per `00-planning-brief.md`) and for the `integration` gate's no-network-egress requirement (`CONSTITUTION.md` §9 #7). E02 must therefore ship the *loop* — start everything, get data flowing, run the gates — plus the documentation that makes it reproducible, which is the concrete mitigation for risk **R10 key-person**.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `make dev`: one command that starts the compose stack (E02-T08), runs the api with `CV_FEED=synthetic`, and starts the `apps/web` Vite dev server against it, with a documented teardown.

- `/README.md` rewritten as a working onboarding path: prerequisites with pinned minimum versions (confirmed by E02-Q02), clone → install → verify → up → dev, plus a troubleshooting section seeded from E02-Q02's findings (WSL filesystem vs `/mnt/c`, port conflicts, Docker integration).
- A "first hour" checklist a new joiner can tick, stored beside the QA artefacts in `docs/plan/qa/`.
- Links, not duplicates: the README points at `AGENTS.md` §4 for commands (C-16.5 — that file owns the command list) and at `CONTRIBUTING.md` for process.

## Out of scope
- The real Bybit adapter, WS ingestion, book reconstruction, bar building — **E08**.
- Recorded real fixtures and the capture/redact pipeline (`03-testing-strategy.md` §4.4) — **E08**; this ticket commits only a small hand-authored sample file.
- CI usage of the synthetic feed (E03 wires it into the `integration` job).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Given a machine with the documented prerequisites and no Bybit credentials
When `make dev` runs
Then the compose stack becomes healthy, the api starts in synthetic-feed mode, the web dev server serves the placeholder route, and no outbound request to any exchange host is made

Given the api in synthetic-feed mode
When a developer inspects the bus metrics exposed at /metrics
Then normalised Trade and Ticker events are being published at the configured rate, and the rate is changeable by an environment variable read through M1 config

Given CV_FEED=live is set without credentials
When the api starts
Then it fails fast with a clear, actionable error rather than starting in a half-configured state

Given a new joiner follows only the README
When they complete the documented path
Then they reach a green `pnpm verify` and a running `make dev` without contacting the scaffold's author, verified by the E02-Q02 charter
```

## Technical notes / design
The generator is intentionally thin: it reads a JSONL sample, maps records to the normalised event dataclasses, and publishes to the bus on a timer with jitter, honouring backpressure from the bounded queues (M5). It must not become a second ingestion implementation — a comment and a Semgrep-visible marker state that it is a test double and that E08 owns the real path. The `CV_FEED` enum lives in M1 `config` alongside `Environment` (E02-T05) so the switch is structural and explicit, never inferred (the same principle the OpenAPI convention C9 applies to `environment`).

## Test plan
- Unit: generator emits well-formed normalised events; rate configuration honoured; backpressure causes drop-or-block per the configured policy rather than unbounded growth; `CV_FEED=live` without credentials raises the documented startup error.
- Integration: `make dev` smoke — stack healthy, events observed on the bus within 10 s, clean shutdown.
- E2E: the existing Playwright placeholder smoke runs against `make dev` rather than a hand-started server, proving the loop is the one the tests use.
- Docs test: E02-Q02's charter is the acceptance evidence for the README.
- Coverage: generator ≥85% (backend threshold).

## Security notes
The synthetic path is also a safety control: it guarantees that development and CI never require, and therefore never hold, real exchange credentials — directly supporting the E02-X01 objective that no real key can appear in the local stack, and the B3 boundary rule (`20-architecture.md` §2.2) that the KEK never resides in WSL. The sample fixture must contain no account identifiers, order ids or keys, enforced by the `packages/fixtures` redaction verify script (E02-T03). `CV_FEED=live` must be impossible to select accidentally: it requires an explicit environment value and explicit credentials, and the startup error must not echo any credential material.

## Accessibility notes
N/A for the backend loop. The README is a documentation surface: it must use proper heading structure and avoid conveying meaning by colour alone, per the spirit of `05-accessibility-standard.md`.

## Performance notes
`make dev` to a usable state ≤150 s cold (compose ≤120 s per E02-T08 plus Vite start). The generator must sustain its configured rate without unbounded memory growth — an early, cheap rehearsal of budget #8 (≤300 MB resident per recorded symbol) although no real symbol load applies yet.

The generator increments the same bus-publish counters the real ingestion path will use, so Grafana panels built in E04 work against synthetic data before E08 lands — a deliberate sequencing win.

body:
## Context
E02 introduces no screens of its own, but it does create `packages/ui` and must wire its **token build** (E02-T03). `16-design-system-brief.md` §2 defines a three-tier token architecture (Tier 1 global/primitive, Tier 2 alias/semantic — the layer `15-component-catalogue.md` entries reference, e.g. `color.buy`, `font.mono`, `space.field.gap` — and Tier 3 component tokens used sparingly), §11 defines the handoff spec (tokens JSON → code) and §13 defines the design-ahead process and sign-off definition. E05 (design system v0, S01–S04, design-led) will author the actual token values; if the *file format, naming and build contract* are not agreed before `packages/ui` is scaffolded, E05 lands two sprints later into a pipeline shaped by an engineer's guess and pays for it in rework across every component. The design-ahead rule (`00-planning-brief.md`: design runs ≥2 sprints ahead) makes S01 the correct slot for this contract, ahead of its consuming work.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A written **handoff contract** (added as a subsection of `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md` §11, not a new doc) specifying: the tokens JSON format (W3C Design Tokens Community Group format), directory layout in `packages/ui/src/tokens/`, the Tier 1/2/3 file split, naming rules and the casing convention, theme file structure for dark (default), light and high-contrast, and the density-mode dimension (`16-design-system-brief.md` §3).

## Context
`03-testing-strategy.md` §11.2 mandates exploratory charters alongside scripted plans. ## Scope / Deliverables
- A 2-session, time-boxed exploratory charter (90 minutes each) executed by a QA/SDET **who did not build the scaffold**, on a machine that has never built this repo:

Explore: missing prerequisite versions, unclear errors, silent failures, path/permission issues when the repo lives on `/mnt/c` versus the WSL filesystem, CRLF/LF damage from `.editorconfig` gaps.
  - Session 2 — *"From zero to running stack"*: `make up`, health checks, `make down`, `make reset`, re-up. Explore: port conflicts with other local services, Docker Desktop integration off, insufficient memory, stale volumes, what happens with no network, what happens with no Bybit credentials (must still work via `CV_FEED=synthetic`).
- Session notes in the charter format of `03-testing-strategy.md` §11.2 (charter, areas explored, risks found, bugs filed, coverage assessment, time split setup/test/bug-reporting).
- Bugs and documentation defects filed with reproduction steps and environment.

- Scripted regression cases (E02-Q01) and the automated regression pack (E02-Q03).
- CI runner environments (E03).
- macOS/native-Windows support — the target is WSL Ubuntu per `20-architecture.md` §5; a finding that something *only* works on one host OS is still reportable.

```gherkin

When they follow only the committed documentation
Then they reach a green `pnpm verify` and a healthy `make up` without asking the scaffold's author a question, or every question asked is filed as a documentation defect

When the gates are run
Then either they pass, or the documentation explicitly warns against that location with a stated reason and the warning is verified to be present

Given both sessions complete
When the charter notes are reviewed
```

Exploratory means unscripted within the charter's boundary: the tester deliberately tries the wrong thing (skip a prerequisite, run from the wrong directory, interrupt an install, start with a port already bound) because those are the real first-day failure modes. title: QA: automated toolchain regression pack guarding the scaffold's gates
body:
## Context
Gates decay. A contract gets an `ignore_imports` exception "just for now", a coverage `omit` entry is added and never removed, a task is renamed and its documentation row rots. `CONSTITUTION.md` C-9.4 forbids lowering thresholds and C-9.3 bounds flaky-test quarantine to 10 working days, but neither is self-enforcing. E02-Q01 verifies the gates once, by hand; this ticket makes that verification **repeatable and automated**, so the guarantee survives every future PR rather than being true only on the day E02 closed.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A regression pack at `tests/toolchain/` (runnable via `pnpm test:toolchain`, included in nightly per C-9.2 and not in the PR-blocking path unless fast enough) asserting:
  1. Every gate name in `CONSTITUTION.md` §9's table is either implemented locally or explicitly registered as CI-only, with an owning epic — no gate silently missing.
  2. Every documented task in `AGENTS.md` §4 resolves in the task graph (reuses `check-agents-commands.mjs`).
  3. Coverage thresholds equal or exceed the §9 values for every package (threshold-guard from E02-T10 run as an assertion, not only as a diff).
  4. The coverage `omit`/exclusion lists carry a dated ticket reference and none is past its stated expiry.
  5. Every `import-linter`/`dependency-cruiser` contract from E02-T06 is present and has zero exceptions; an added exception fails the pack unless accompanied by an ADR reference.
  6. Every `@flaky`-marked test has a ticket reference and a quarantine start date within 10 working days (C-9.3).
  7. Compose invariants: all published ports bound to loopback, all images digest-pinned, all services healthchecked.
- A short README explaining how to extend the pack when a new gate is added (so E03/E04 add to it rather than around it).

## Out of scope
- Re-implementing the gates themselves (owned by T06/T10/T08).
- CI scheduling and nightly workflow definition (E03).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Given the regression pack
When `pnpm test:toolchain` runs on the merged scaffold
Then every assertion passes and the run completes in under 3 minutes

Given a coverage threshold is lowered from 85 to 70 in any package config
When the pack runs
Then it fails citing C-9.4 and naming the package

Given an `ignore_imports` exception is added to an import-linter contract without an ADR reference
When the pack runs
Then it fails naming the contract and the missing ADR

Given a test is marked @flaky with a quarantine date older than 10 working days
When the pack runs
Then it fails citing C-9.3 and the owning ticket

Given a new compose service is added without a healthcheck or with a mutable image tag
When the pack runs
Then it fails naming the service and the violated invariant
```

title: Security: STRIDE threat model for the monorepo supply chain and local dev stack

## Context
`00-planning-brief.md` requires a STRIDE threat model per epic, and `30-release-roadmap.md` §4.4 lists "STRIDE models complete for E03 (supply chain), E08 (exchange boundary), E09 (auth/RBAC)" as an R0 quality gate. E02 is where the supply chain is actually *created* — lockfiles, registries, lifecycle scripts, base images, git hooks, a local stack with datastores — so its model must land in S01, before E03 formalises the pipeline on top of it, and must hand E03 a ready list of controls to implement as CI jobs. `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.1 requires the STRIDE kickoff to be scheduled for any epic touching this ground.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A STRIDE model at `docs/plan/security/E02-threat-model.md` decomposing: developer workstation → git → package registries (npm, PyPI) → lockfiles → build (Turbo/uv/Docker) → local compose stack (postgres, questdb, prometheus, grafana, minio) → the WSL/Windows host boundary.
- Data-flow diagram (mermaid) with trust boundaries, reusing and extending `20-architecture.md` §2.2 boundaries B2 (host↔WSL) and B4 (renderer↔Electron main).
- Threat enumeration with at least: **S** — registry account/typosquat impersonation, forged commit identity; **T** — lockfile tampering, malicious postinstall/`prepare` script, mutable base-image tag substitution, hook tampering; **R** — unsigned commits/artefacts; **I** — secrets committed to git, `.env` leakage, recorded fixtures containing credentials, services bound to `0.0.0.0` reachable from the LAN via WSL portproxy; **D** — dependency-confusion outage, oversized image/volume filling the dev disk during a soak; **E** — container running as root, docker-socket mount, renderer→Node escalation via disabled Electron hardening.
- For each threat: likelihood/impact rating, the control, **where the control is implemented** (ticket key in E02 or E03), and the residual risk with an accept/mitigate decision.
- Abuse cases written as concrete scenarios (e.g. "a compromised transitive npm dependency adds a postinstall script that exfiltrates `~/.ssh`"; "a contributor commits a real `.env` with a Bybit demo key"; "an attacker on the same LAN reaches QuestDB because a port was bound to 0.0.0.0").
- Findings routed into `32-risk-register.md` where they represent programme-level risk.

## Out of scope
- Modelling the application's runtime threats (exchange boundary is E08; auth/RBAC is E09; key vault is E27) — this model stops at the scaffold and local stack.
- Implementing the scanners (E02-X02/E03) — this ticket specifies them.
- Pen-testing (R4, E43).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Given the threat model document
When the Security engineer reviews it
Then every STRIDE category has at least one enumerated threat with a rated likelihood/impact, a named control and an owning ticket key

Given a threat whose control is not implemented anywhere in E02 or E03
When the model is finalised
Then either a new ticket is filed or the residual risk is explicitly accepted with the Owner's recorded sign-off — never left blank

Given the abuse case "service bound to 0.0.0.0 on WSL"
When the model is traced to its control
Then it points at the automated loopback-binding assertion in E02-T08 and the regression assertion in E02-Q03

Given the model
When E03 plans its supply-chain jobs
Then every scanner it configures (CodeQL, Semgrep, Bandit, pip-audit, npm audit, gitleaks, Trivy, license-check) traces back to at least one threat in this model
```

## Technical notes / design
Model at the data-flow level, not the file level, so it stays valid as the scaffold evolves. Explicitly record the two deliberate exceptions made in E02 and their compensating controls: the husky `prepare` lifecycle script (E02-T07) and the `packages/fixtures` redaction requirement (E02-T03). Note that the KEK for API-key envelope encryption lives in the **host OS keychain, never in WSL** (`20-architecture.md` §2.2 B3) — the local dev stack must therefore never be a place where real keys can appear, which is why default credentials are `CHANGE_ME` and the bootstrap refuses them outside the dev profile.

## Test plan
N/A as code. Verification: (a) Security engineer review; (b) a traceability check that every control names an existing ticket key; (c) each abuse case is either automated (by E02-T08/T06/Q03 assertions) or listed as a manual check in E02-X02.

## Security notes
This ticket *is* the security artefact. Data classification for E02's scope: **no production data, no PII, no live keys** — the model's job is to keep it that way by making "a real credential in this stack" structurally impossible rather than merely discouraged.

## Accessibility notes

Controls must not push the pipeline past R0 exit criterion 2 (≤15 min commit→dev). Where a scanner is slow (CodeQL, full-history gitleaks), the model states whether it belongs on the PR path or the nightly path (C-9.2) and why.

title: Security: baseline SAST, secrets, SCA and license scanning configuration for the scaffold

## Context
`CONSTITUTION.md` §9 makes `sast` (#10 CodeQL + Semgrep with custom rules incl. **withdrawal-endpoint ban**, secret-leak and raw-SQL rules, + Bandit), `sca` (#11 pip-audit + npm audit, zero high/critical without an approved expiring exception), `secrets-scan` (#12 gitleaks full-history + trufflehog on the diff, any finding fails) and `license-check` (#14 allowlist MIT/Apache-2.0/BSD-2-3/ISC/MPL-2.0/Python-2.0/Unlicense/CC0, denylist GPL/AGPL/SSPL/BUSL, unknown = fail) blocking checks. E03 owns the workflow files; but the **configurations, custom rules, baselines and suppression policy** must live with the code and be runnable locally, or E03 will be wiring jobs to tools nobody has tuned. Doing it now also means the very first dependency set is scanned before it becomes load-bearing.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `semgrep/` rule pack with CandleViewer-specific rules derived from the Constitution: (a) **withdrawal-endpoint ban** — any code path referencing Bybit withdrawal/transfer/funding endpoints fails (C-1.2 item 5, C-2.7); (b) Bybit-identifier ban outside `services/api/candleviewer/exchange/bybit/`, `packages/protocol` enums, docs and config keys (C-2.2); (c) raw-SQL/string-interpolated query detection; (d) secret-shaped literal detection; (e) a rule flagging any log call that passes a settings object or a field matching `(key|secret|token|password|signature)`.
- CodeQL configuration (JS/TS + Python) with the query suites selected and a documented, dated suppression policy.
- Bandit config (already added in E02-T02) tuned: excluded paths, severity floor, and no blanket `# nosec` without a dated justification comment — enforced by a Semgrep rule.
- gitleaks config + a clean full-history baseline; trufflehog diff-mode config; `.gitignore` verified for `.env`, `*.pem`, `*.key`, coverage and build output.
- `pip-audit` and `npm audit --audit-level=high` wrappers plus the **exception file format**: every exception has a CVE, a reason, an owner and an expiry date, and an expired exception fails the check.
- `license-check` configuration implementing the exact allow/deny lists of §9 #14, with unknown-license = fail, and a generated SBOM (CycloneDX) per ecosystem.
- A single `make security` / `pnpm security` entry point running everything runnable locally, documented in `AGENTS.md` §4.

## Out of scope
- GitHub Actions job definitions, Dependabot configuration, code scanning alert routing, Trivy container scanning in CI (#13) — **E03** (though the Trivy *policy file* is authored here if it is a repo-level config).
- DAST/OWASP ZAP (nightly, E03/E43) and pen-testing (E43).
- Remediating findings in application code that does not exist yet.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Given the scaffold
When `make security` runs
Then SAST, secrets, SCA and license checks all execute and report zero high/critical findings on the baseline

Given a test file containing a call to a Bybit withdrawal endpoint
When Semgrep runs
Then the withdrawal-endpoint-ban rule fires with a message citing C-1.2 and C-2.7

Given the string "bybit" is introduced in services/api/candleviewer/oms/service.py
When Semgrep runs
Then the adapter-isolation rule fires citing C-2.2

Given a committed file containing an AWS-style key or a Bybit API secret pattern
When gitleaks runs over the full history
Then the scan fails and identifies the file and commit

Given an SCA exception whose expiry date has passed
When the SCA wrapper runs
Then the check fails naming the expired exception, its CVE and its owner

Given a dependency licensed under AGPL-3.0
When license-check runs
Then it fails, and an unknown/unparseable license also fails rather than being ignored
```

## Technical notes / design
Custom Semgrep rules must be unit-tested using Semgrep's own `--test` fixtures (a rule that never fires is worse than no rule — it manufactures confidence). The withdrawal-endpoint ban is the single highest-value rule in the repository: `CONSTITUTION.md` C-1.2 item 5 puts withdrawal/transfer/funding operations out of scope "of any kind, through any code path", and the architecture's startup self-check refuses trading mode if a stored key has withdrawal enabled (`20-architecture.md` §2.2 B3); the Semgrep rule is the *static* half of that defence and must match endpoint paths, method names and the Bybit-specific asset-transfer nomenclature. Suppressions (`# nosec`, `// nosemgrep`, gitleaks allowlist entries) require a dated justification and an owner, checked by a meta-rule.

## Test plan
- Unit: Semgrep rule tests with positive and negative fixtures for each of the five custom rules.
- Unit: SCA exception-file parser tests (valid, missing field, expired, future expiry).
- Integration: `make security` full run on the scaffold; a deliberately seeded secret in a scratch branch confirmed to fail gitleaks (then removed and the history of that scratch branch discarded).
- Integration: a temporarily added AGPL dependency confirmed to fail license-check.
- Coverage: wrapper scripts counted under the relevant package thresholds.

## Security notes
This ticket *is* a security control set, implementing the mitigations enumerated in E02-X01 for Tampering (malicious dependency), Information Disclosure (committed secrets, logged credentials) and Elevation (raw SQL → injection). Note the deliberate ordering: the gitleaks **full-history** baseline is established now, while history is short and cheap to scan; establishing it later is materially more expensive and risks grandfathering a real leak. Data classification: the scanners themselves must not upload source to third-party services — CodeQL runs in GitHub's own environment (already the code host), and Semgrep runs with the local rule pack, not the cloud platform, per the "no third-party SaaS that receives market, order or account data" guardrail (C-1.2 item 6) applied conservatively to source as well.

The locally runnable set (`make security`) must complete in ≤5 min; CodeQL and full-history gitleaks may exceed this and are allocated to the CI/nightly split decided in E02-X01, protecting R0 exit criterion 2 (≤15 min pipeline).

All scanners emit SARIF where supported, written to `reports/security/` so E03 can upload to code scanning and E04 can trend finding counts by severity.
